items: What did you experience with God this week?

data.html:
20 Just then a woman who had been subject to bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the edge of his cloak. 21 She said to herself, “If I only touch his cloak, I will be healed.”

22Jesus turned and saw her. “Take heart, daughter,” he said, “your faith has healed you.” And the woman was healed at that moment.

27 As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed him, calling out, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”

28When he had gone indoors, the blind men came to him, and he asked them, “Do you believe that I am able to do this?”

“Yes, Lord,” they replied.

29Then he touched their eyes and said, “According to your faith let it be done to you”;

items:
Everyone by themselves:
  • What words or phrases stick out now? Are there any differences to what you noticed before?
  • Why do you feel drawn to those words or phrases?
  • What could God be telling you?
  • What can you learn about mankind?
What can we learn about faith from the woman and the two blind men?
God reacts to your faith. For what situation or area in your life do you need faith?
To have faith also means to act. Where does the Holy Spirit encou­rage you to take steps of faith?
Note this down and then share in groups of two or three.

data.text: ▶ You can pray the following prayer: “Thank you, dear Heavenly Father, that You have given me Your Holy Spirit, who teaches me to trust and have faith. Forgive me, where I trusted my experiences more than Your Word and thus have acted in unbelief. Train me so I can grow in faith. I want to learn to see things from Your perspective in every situation, to focus on what happens in the spiritual realm and not the visible realm. Help me to understand Your Word and Your perspective more and more.”

Faith means that we accept and proclaim what God thinks about a situation and what is possible for him. Because to have faith means to know that the visible realm – our limitations, experiences, sorrows – are not the only reality. The spiritual realm is the place where the script for your life is written. The visible realm is only what happens on the screen. Abraham showed us what faith is. He had to wait a really long time before he could have a son. All aspects of Abraham’s and Sarah’s lives had long been indicating that they would not be able get a son. But Abraham persisted and put his trust in God and His promise.
To us, God’s Word, the written and living Word (Jesus), is the crucial tool for us to grow in faith. Because it transmits the real truth about...

items: …what God is like – He for whom everything is possible, who fights for us, who hears the cries of our hearts (Psalm 34:7), our provider, prince of peace, doctor, shelter, wisdom, beginning and the end, and so on.
…and what he did for us – we are accepted, loved, his children, envoys, he made us kings and priests, and so on.
God’s Word: Know who God is and what He did for us.
Prayer: Proclaim this over you or a situation you’re in (“Heavenly Father, you are…” and “in your eyes, I am…”).

data.text: Remember. If we hear God’s word (even from our own lips) and hold on to it perseveringly, it will bring fruit. It will release faith for God’s plans in our lives (Romans 10:14; Luke 8:15).
